_meta.source: Music Architect FX Variant System — psychoacoustic timbral flavors
_meta.principle: Each variant applies a chain_overlay that modifies 2-4 effect chain slots per track. NEUTRAL always has an empty overlay (it IS the genre reference). BRIGHT emphasizes air shelf, shorter reverb pre-delay, less saturation drive. DARK emphasizes tape saturation, longer reverb tails, darker EQ curves. All parameters derive from Fletcher-Munson equal-loudness contours, ITU-R BS.1770, and EBU R128.
_meta.note: chain_overlay format is identical to chain_delta in instrument_palettes.json

instrument_classes.label: Synth Lead
instrument_classes.description: GM 80-87 (Square, Sawtooth, Calliope, etc.) — harmonically dense electronic tones
instrument_classes.science: Sawtooth/square waves contain all harmonics up to Nyquist. Adding reverb and saturation to already-dense spectra raises the 300-3000 Hz noise floor (BDRA P4 density principle). Adjustments: reduce reverb wet signal and saturation drive to prevent harmonic mud.

melody.note: Synth lead already has full harmonic stack — reduce saturation drive to prevent inter-harmonic distortion products
melody.params: Drive +1 dB, Mix 15%, HF roll-off 12 kHz

melody.note: Harmonic density creates its own spatial impression — reduce reverb wet by ~4% to preserve transient definition
melody.params: Decay 1.1 s, Pre-delay 22 ms, HPF 500 Hz, LPF 7 kHz, Mix 8%

instrument_classes.label: Synth Pad
instrument_classes.description: GM 88-95 (New Age, Warm, Polysynth, Choir, etc.) — slow-attack evolving textures
instrument_classes.science: Pad instruments have BDRA A=3 (attack >100ms). The slow onset means the compressor's attack phase does not interfere with transients. Longer reverb is perceptually coherent because the source's own attack is already slow. Adjustments: extend reverb time and slow compressor attack to match the natural envelope.

pads.note: Slow pad attack (A=3 BDRA) — faster compressor attack would pump unnecessarily; slow to 15ms
pads.params: 3 voices, Rate 0.22 Hz, Depth 9 ms, Mix 45%, Spread 100%

pads.note: Extend reverb decay to complement slow-attack pad — perceptual continuity across the slow onset
pads.params: Decay 4.5 s, Pre-delay 0 ms, HPF 350 Hz, Mix 32%

instrument_classes.label: String Ensemble
instrument_classes.description: GM 48-51 (String Ensemble 1/2, Synth Strings 1/2) — bowed string textures
instrument_classes.science: Bowed strings have natural vibrato (±25 cents, 5-7 Hz) and dynamic variation that compressors destroy. Tube saturation adds 2nd-harmonic warmth consistent with the overtone series of real strings. Reverb should use hall (not plate) because bowed string performance spaces are large halls. Adjustments: lower compression ratio, swap tape for tube saturation.

melody.note: Reduce compression ratio for string ensemble — natural string dynamics should breathe; 2:1 preserves expressiveness
melody.params: Ratio 2:1, Thr -16 dBFS, Attack 15 ms, Release 120 ms, Knee 8 dB, GR 2-4 dB
Drive +1.5 dB, Mix 18%, 2nd harmonic bias
melody.note: Tape HF roll-off cuts string overtones above 8 kHz — tube saturation adds warmth without frequency loss

instrument_classes.label: Choir / Voice
instrument_classes.description: GM 52-54 (Choir Aahs, Voice Oohs, Synth Voice) — vocal formant textures
instrument_classes.science: Human voice formants (F1: 200-1000 Hz, F2: 500-2500 Hz) are degraded by ping-pong delay reflections which create comb-filtering in the formant region. Hall reverb is perceptually appropriate (choirs perform in large spaces). Single-tap delay is safer than ping-pong for formant-heavy sources. Adjustments: swap ping-pong delay to single-tap, extend hall reverb.

melody.params: 1/8D = 45000/BPM ms, Feedback 18%, Mix 10%, HPF 400 Hz, LPF 6 kHz, mono
melody.note: Swap ping-pong for mono single-tap delay — ping-pong comb-filters vocal formant frequencies (F1-F2 200-2500 Hz)
Extend hall reverb — choir/voice sources are perceptually expected in large reverberant spaces
melody.params: Decay 1.8 s, Pre-delay 28 ms, HPF 350 Hz, LPF 8 kHz, Mix 16%

instrument_classes.label: Electric Piano
instrument_classes.description: GM 4-5 (Electric Piano 1/2, FM E.Piano) — hammer-struck electric piano tones
instrument_classes.science: Rhodes and Wurlitzer electric pianos were historically amplified through tube amplifiers (Fender, Vox), giving them a characteristic 2nd-harmonic warmth. Plate reverb was the studio standard for electric piano (EMT 140 plates widely used in 1970s-80s sessions). Tape HF roll-off removes the natural bell-like overtones above 6 kHz. Adjustments: swap tape for tube saturation, recommend plate reverb character.

chords.note: Electric piano historically combined with chorus/phaser — reduce rate for cleaner sound under fast BPM
chords.params: Rate 0.28 Hz, Depth 6 ms, Mix 16%, 2 voices, Spread 60%

melody.params: Drive +2 dB, Mix 20%, 2nd harmonic bias
melody.note: Electric piano through tube amplifier is historically authentic — tape HF roll-off removes characteristic bell overtones above 8 kHz
Plate reverb character for electric piano — EMT 140 plate was the standard reverb choice in classic recordings
melody.params: Decay 1.2 s, Pre-delay 15 ms, HPF 400 Hz, LPF 9 kHz, Mix 14%

instrument_classes.label: Brass / Synth Brass
instrument_classes.description: GM 56-63 (Trumpet, Trombone, Brass Section, Synth Brass) — harmonic-rich bright tones
instrument_classes.science: Brass instruments contain strong 3rd-through-9th harmonics concentrated in 1-4 kHz. Boosting the air shelf above 10 kHz adds piercing brightness to an already bright source. Brass should use a shorter reverb pre-delay than strings because brass attacks are fast (BDRA A=0-1); longer pre-delays make the attack sound disconnected from the room. Adjustments: reduce air shelf boost, shorten reverb pre-delay.

melody.note: Reduce air shelf — brass already has strong 3rd-9th harmonics in 1-4 kHz; adding 10 kHz shelf creates piercing harshness
melody.params: +1 dB high shelf @10 kHz; Ceiling -7 dBFS

melody.note: Shorter reverb pre-delay for fast brass attack (BDRA A=0-1) — pre-delay >25ms disconnects attack from room response
melody.params: Decay 1.0 s, Pre-delay 14 ms, HPF 450 Hz, LPF 7 kHz, Mix 9%
